transcript: Speaker A: 'I don't know nothing' ye sentence sahi hai ya galat? Agar tumne bola sahi, toh tumhari English mein ek bohot badi galti hai. Ye double negative hai, 'I don't know anything' sahi hai. Aur ye galti tum roz karte ho bina jaane. Negative sentences matlab jab tum na, nahi, mat, kabhi nahi bolte ho English mein, ye sabse zyada galtiyan hone wali jagah hai. Rule 1: Do, Does ke sath Not. 'I do not like' sahi, 'I does not like' galat. 'He does not know' sahi, 'He do not know' galat. Singular ke sath does, plural aur I, You ke sath do. Rule 2: Am, Is, Are ke sath Not. 'I am not happy', 'She is not here', 'They are not coming'. Yahan do, does nahi lagta, am, is, are ke baad directly not. Rule 3: Double negative mat lagao. 'I don't have no money' galat, 'I don't have any money' sahi. Hindi mein double negative chalti hai 'mujhe kuch nahi chahiye', English mein nahi chalti. Rule 4: Never ke sath not mat lagao. 'I don't never go' galat, 'I never go' sahi. Never already negative hai, not lagane ki zaroorat nahi. [Is the sentence 'I don't know nothing' right or wrong? If you said right, there is a big mistake in your English. This is a double negative; 'I don't know anything' is correct. And you make this mistake daily without knowing. Negative sentences, meaning when you say no, not, never in English, are where most mistakes happen. Rule 1: Not with Do, Does. 'I do not like' is correct, 'I does not like' is wrong. 'He does not know' is correct, 'He do not know' is wrong. Does with singular, do with plural and I, You. Rule 2: Not with Am, Is, Are. 'I am not happy', 'She is not here', 'They are not coming'. Do or does is not used here, directly not after am, is, are. Rule 3: Do not use double negatives. 'I don't have no money' is wrong, 'I don't have any money' is correct. Double negatives work in Hindi like 'mujhe kuch nahi chahiye', but not in English. Rule 4: Do not use not with never. 'I don't never go' is wrong, 'I never go' is correct. Never is already negative, no need to add not.
